_comment: Approved catalog-serialization exceptions to the B-23 fidelity gate.
An entry here is NOT a waiver. verify-baseline.sh still detects the
difference and asserts it is EXACTLY this one, in both directions: if the
production value moves, if the local value moves, if a second difference
appears in the same file, or if this difference stops appearing, the gate
FAILS. A stale allowlist is a failure, not a pass.
Admissible only for a difference individually demonstrated to be
PostgreSQL normalization or catalog history rather than a semantic or
schema difference. Never add a broad whitespace or parenthesis rule: that
would conceal genuine future differences, which is the opposite of what

exceptions.production: CHECK (((account_id IS NULL) OR (((char_length(account_id) >= 3) AND (char_length(account_id) <= 24)) AND (account_id ~ '^[a-z0-9_]+$'::text))))
exceptions.local: CHECK (((account_id IS NULL) OR ((char_length(account_id) >= 3) AND (char_length(account_id) <= 24) AND (account_id ~ '^[a-z0-9_]+$'::text))))
exceptions.equivalence: Logically identical. AND is associative; production stores a left-nested two-way AND, local a flat three-way AND. No query, constraint check or error message can distinguish them.
evidence: Both servers are PostgreSQL 17.6 (verified with select version() on each), so this is not a major-version difference.
Feeding production's own emitted expression straight back into PostgreSQL 17.6 produces the FLAT form, so production's representation cannot be round-tripped from its own rendering.
A RIGHT-nested source expression IS preserved verbatim, which shows the parser flattens left-nesting specifically rather than normalising all nesting.
Therefore no migration SQL can produce production's catalog representation on 17.6; it is inherited catalog history, almost certainly carried through a major-version upgrade.
exceptions.removal_condition: Remove this entry if production's stored representation ever becomes reproducible from SQL — for example after a schema change that rewrites the constraint. The gate will fail the moment that happens, which is the intended prompt to revisit it.
